content: The American Association for Laboratory Animal Science (AALAS) is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit membership organization that was established in 1950. Its primary purpose is to serve as a platform for the exchange of information and expertise related to the care and use of laboratory animals. The organization has approximately 12,000 members, including individuals, institutions, commercial entities, and affiliates. The national office of AALAS is located in Memphis, Tennessee. National Meeting Since 1950, AALAS has hosted an annual National Meeting every fall. This five-day event includes workshops, lectures, poster sessions, and exhibits, which are open to both members and non-members. The program is designed to cover topics relevant to the entire membership. Exhibitors at the event have the opportunity to engage with AALAS members from academia, research institutions, government organizations, and commercial companies. Each year, eight professional and technical awards are presented to recognize excellence in the field of laboratory animal science. The AALAS National Meeting is the largest global gathering of professionals involved in the production, care, and use of laboratory animals. Publications AALAS publishes two scientific journals and two newsletters. These publications are produced at the AALAS national office in Memphis, Tennessee. Comparative Medicine (CM): This is an international, bi-monthly journal focused on comparative and experimental medicine. It is a leading English-language publication in the field and is ranked in the upper third of all scientific journals by the Science Citation Index. The journal aims to advance knowledge in comparative medicine and laboratory animal science by publishing scholarly articles on topics such as animal models, animal biology, laboratory animal medicine, pathology, behavior, biotechnology, and related subjects. It also includes reports, reviews, and informed opinions on the humane care and use of laboratory animals. Comparative Medicine is indexed in Index Medicus. Dr. Linda Toth of Southern Illinois University School of Medicine serves as the editor-in-chief, while Dr. Ravi Tolwani of Rockefeller University is the associate editor. Journal of the American Association for Laboratory Animal Science (JAALAS): This bi-monthly journal serves as the official communication platform for AALAS. It includes a section of peer-reviewed articles and a section dedicated to AALAS association news. The mission of the refereed section is to disseminate high-quality, peer-reviewed information on topics such as animal biology, technology, facility operations, management, and compliance, all of which are relevant to AALAS members. The journal's title was changed in 2006 from Contemporary Topics in Laboratory Animal Science (CT) to JAALAS. Dr. Linda Toth is the editor-in-chief, and Dr. Susan Compton of Yale University serves as the associate editor. AALAS in Action: This bi-monthly newsletter is designed to enhance communication with national and branch members of AALAS. Recipients are encouraged to reproduce parts or all of its content. Tech Talk: This bi-monthly publication promotes the dissemination of professional information and technology to individuals interested in laboratory animal science. It also facilitates the global pursuit of knowledge in animal care methodologies. Certification AALAS offers a technician certification program that certifies three levels of technical knowledge. The Technician Certification Registry is a voluntary program that allows technicians to demonstrate a current and credible level of knowledge. Additionally, the Certified Manager of Animal Resources (CMAR) program is designed to enhance competency and professionalism in the field of animal resources management. Certified Manager of Animal Resources (CMAR): The CMAR designation requires passing a series of four examinations: three exams administered by the Institute for Certified Professional Managers (ICPM) and the Animal Resources Exam offered by AALAS. Achieving the CMAR designation signifies professionalism in animal resources management. To maintain their certification, CMAR recipients must pay an annual re-certification fee and complete a specified number of continuing education credits to stay updated on the latest management techniques and theories. Technician Certification: The AALAS Certification and Registry Board (CRB) certifies three levels of technician competence: Assistant Laboratory Animal Technician (ALAT), Laboratory Animal Technician (LAT), and Laboratory Animal Technologist (LATG). These certifications are widely recognized and utilized across various fields of laboratory animal care. Institute for Laboratory Animal Management (ILAM) The Institute for Laboratory Animal Management (ILAM) is an educational program developed by AALAS to provide instruction in management concepts applicable to the laboratory animal science industry. It also aims to enhance communication, team building, and networking among colleagues with shared interests. Over the years, the roles of directors, managers, and supervisors of laboratory animal facilities have become increasingly complex, requiring them to interpret social, political, and economic environments while using administrative and technical skills to maintain and improve animal care and use programs. Most individuals in these positions were trained in biological and veterinary sciences and must seek additional training in management skills to fulfill their administrative roles effectively. AALAS Learning Library The AALAS Learning Library offers essential training for technicians, veterinarians, managers, Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) members, and investigators working with animals in research or educational settings. The courses emphasize proper handling, care, and use of animals and are designed to help individuals prepare for AALAS certification, meet regulatory training mandates, and improve their knowledge in technical areas. AALAS Foundation The AALAS Foundation is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization that provides funding for projects aimed at promoting awareness of biomedical research and its contributions to society. Through the Foundation, AALAS offers a variety of public outreach tools, including flyers, posters, websites, videos, DVDs, and classroom materials.
